title: Control plane: drift detection for Dedicated pools (desired vs actual runtime settings)
author: Vikram Singh
description: Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation sprint, we want a durable way to detect when a Dedicated pool has diverged from its intended configuration after it has been marked Ready (or while it is in Validating). This PR adds a control-plane drift detection job that compares the pool's desired runtime config (the versioned config we persist at provisioning time) against the actual runtime settings reported by the cluster agents / runtime introspection endpoint. Drift is surfaced in new control plane API fields and (behind a feature flag) in the Console UI as a small banner + a per-pool drift summary for operators. What this includes: (1) New drift detector worker that runs periodically and on-demand (API-triggered) per pool; (2) Canonicalization + stable hashing of config payloads to reduce false positives (e.g., map ordering, defaulted fields); (3) A set of initial drift rules focused on runtime/serving-critical knobs: runtime chart version, model runtime image tag, batching settings, kv-cache settings, quantization profile, request limits, and a small allowlist of known-dynamic fields (timestamps, node-local paths, ephemeral tokens); (4) Control plane storage for drift state + last_checked_at + summary counts; (5) API additions: PoolStatus now includes drift_status (NONE|DETECTED|UNKNOWN), drift_summary, and drift_items (bounded list, capped to avoid large payloads); (6) Metrics/events: drift_check_duration_seconds (histogram), drift_detected_total (counter), drift_items_total (counter) with cardinality safeguards; (7) Operator UX: CLI and UI can link to a JSON blob with the normalized desired and observed fields (redacted) and suggested remediation (re-run validation, re-apply helm values, or pause routing). Notes/limitations: This is intentionally conservative; we only compare a subset of settings that are deterministic and tied to availability/perf. We do not attempt to compare full Helm values or node-level OS packages in this PR (golden image integrity is handled elsewhere). Security: observed config snapshot is redacted server-side (secrets/token-like strings) and stored with a 7-day TTL; only admin/operator roles can fetch the detailed drift payload. Rollout: gated by feature flag control_plane.drift_detection.enabled (default off in prod, on in staging). Follow-ups: expand rule set to include networking/timeouts and rollout policy mismatches; wire drift banner into the Dedicated readiness dashboard.
commits: control-plane: add drift detector worker + scheduling
control-plane: normalize desired/observed runtime config and compute drift set
api: add drift fields to PoolStatus and admin endpoints for details
observability: add drift metrics + structured events
console: feature-flagged UI banner + operator drilldown link
tests: unit tests for canonicalization + drift rules; integration test with fake agent snapshot
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Love the direction. Two questions: (1) How do we avoid flapping when agents report defaulted values differently? (2) Can we bound drift_items so we don’t blow up PoolStatus payloads? Also please confirm this won’t block Ready transitions by default.

Vikram Singh (author): (1) Added a normalization layer that applies the same defaults we use at config ingest (see normalize.go). Also introduced canonical JSON serialization before hashing; we only diff normalized structs. (2) drift_items is capped at 50 with a summary count; API docs updated. And yes—this is informational only; it does not change Ready gating in this PR.

Ravi Menon (review): For routing safety: if drift is DETECTED, do we want to automatically de-advertise capacity? I’m ok with informational now, but we should at least emit a metric we can alert on, and make sure the routing integration doesn’t accidentally treat DETECTED as Unready.

Vikram Singh (author): Added drift_detected_total + a gauge-like counter per pool via events; alerting can be handled in observability-pack. Routing behavior unchanged; PoolStatus.drift_status is separate from readiness_state. I’ll open a follow-up to optionally gate advertising behind a policy later.

Benji Okafor (review): Please document the allowlist of dynamic fields and make sure we don’t accidentally compare secrets. Also: can we reuse the config schema canonicalizer from the validation library?

Vikram Singh (author): Added redact.go with token/secret-like regexes + explicit field-level redaction; detailed payload endpoint is admin-only. Documented allowlist at top of rules.go. Re: canonicalizer—good call; I imported the shared canonical JSON utility used by schema validation (no new copy/paste).

Rafael Mendes (review): Operationally, I want a way to trigger this on demand when a pool looks weird, and I want the job to fail ‘softly’ (UNKNOWN) rather than raising incidents if agent snapshots are missing. Also: add a runbook pointer in the error message.

Vikram Singh (author): Added admin endpoint POST /admin/pools/{id}/drift-check to run immediately. If agent snapshot missing or stale >30m, we set UNKNOWN and include a reason code; no paging in this service. Error messages include a short runbook pointer string (will be linked in Confluence separately).

Allison Grant (review): Metrics look fine, but please ensure low-cardinality labels (no pool_id). Suggest: emit structured events with pool_id but keep metrics aggregated by region + sku + drift_type. Also ensure payload TTL cleanup is in place.
Vikram Singh (author): Updated metrics to only label by region, sku, and drift_category. Pool identifiers are only in structured logs/events. Added TTL cleanup via existing janitor worker (7 days).
Ethan Park (final): Approved. Please keep the feature flag off in prod until we validate false positive rate in staging.
Vikram Singh (author): Ack—flag default remains off in prod; staging enabled in env config.
release_notes: Control plane now detects and reports configuration drift for Dedicated pools (feature-flagged).
New PoolStatus fields: drift_status, drift_summary, drift_items (bounded).
New metrics/events for drift checks to support operator alerting and dashboards.
